same_change.instructions: You are shown two pull requests from the same repository, A and B. Decide how A relates to B. 'same': A and B implement the same change or fix the same problem in essentially the same way, so merging both would be redundant. 'subset': A is a strict part of B or B of A; merging the larger one makes the smaller unnecessary. 'related': they touch the same area or feature but do different work; both could merge. 'unrelated': different work.

criteria.same: Same change or same fix; redundant to merge both
criteria.subset: One is contained in the other
criteria.related: Same area, different work; both could land

assumption_conflict.instructions: You are shown two pull requests from the same repository, A and B, each with the premises its author declared (what the change takes for granted). Decide whether they can land independently. 'conflict': A and B assume contradictory things about the same target, or one changes a target the other assumes unchanged, so merging both as written would break one of them or require rework. 'depends': one can only be correct after the other has merged (it builds on, rebases on, or needs the other's change). 'independent': both can merge in either order without affecting each other's correctness.

criteria.conflict: Contradictory premises about the same target, or one changes what the other assumes; both cannot land as written
criteria.depends: One needs the other merged first
criteria.independent: Either order, no effect on each other
